findings.title: IDOR: any user can read any note
findings.anchor: db.execute("SELECT id, owner_id, title, body, updated_at FROM notes WHERE id = ?", (note_id,))
findings.notes: GET /notes/{note_id} depends on get_current_user but never compares note.owner_id with user.id, so any signed-in user (in any organization) can read every note by iterating ids. PUT and DELETE in the same file do the check. Fix: add `AND owner_id = ?` (or compare after loading) and return 404.

findings.title: SQL injection in note search (f-string query)
findings.notes: The query string `q` is interpolated into the SQL on the previous line (`LIKE '%{q}%'`) and executed here. `q=%') OR 1=1 --` drops the owner_id filter and returns every user's notes; UNION payloads read other tables. Fix: `title LIKE ? OR body LIKE ?` with bound parameters.

findings.title: Insecure deserialization of the preferences cookie (pickle)
findings.notes: The notes_prefs cookie is client-controlled and unsigned; pickle.loads on it runs arbitrary code (a `__reduce__` payload) on the server for any signed-in user. Fix: store preferences as JSON validated with the Preferences model (or server-side), and sign the cookie if it must carry state.

findings.title: OS command injection in host ping diagnostic
findings.notes: The request body's `host` is formatted into a shell command; `example.com; cat /etc/passwd` or `$(curl ...)` runs arbitrary commands. Any signed-in user can call it. Fix: validate the host as an IP address or hostname and run `subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", "-W", "2", "--", host])` without a shell.

findings.title: SSRF in link preview
findings.notes: Any http(s) URL from the request is fetched server-side, following redirects; the scheme check does not stop internal hosts (http://127.0.0.1:8000/..., http://169.254.169.254/...). Title and description of the response are returned. Fix: resolve and block private/loopback/link-local addresses, disable redirects or re-check each hop, and restrict ports.

findings.title: Tenant isolation: organization id taken from the request body
findings.notes: POST /reports/activity checks that the caller is an admin, but of their own organization; the report is then built for `payload.org_id` from the body instead of `user.org_id`. An admin of any org can list member emails and activity of every other org. Fix: use user.org_id and drop org_id from the request (or verify it equals user.org_id).

findings.title: Hard-coded SECRET_KEY
findings.notes: SECRET_KEY signs the itsdangerous bearer tokens (app/auth.py); anyone who has the source can mint a token for any user id. Fix: read it from the environment or a secret manager and rotate it.

findings.title: Vulnerable dependency: PyYAML 5.3
findings.notes: PyYAML before 5.4 allows arbitrary code execution through full_load/FullLoader (CVE-2020-1747, CVE-2020-14343). The app itself uses safe_load, but the pinned version is still vulnerable. Fix: upgrade to 5.4 or later (6.x).

findings.title: Vulnerable dependency: requests 2.19.0
findings.notes: requests 2.19.0 has known advisories: Authorization header leaked on https-to-http redirects (CVE-2018-18074, fixed in 2.20.0), Proxy-Authorization leak (CVE-2023-32681) and verify=False persisting across a session (CVE-2024-35195). Fix: upgrade to a current 2.32.x release.
